content_of_post_to_answer: How do childhood experiences with unmet needs affect my current feelings of shame in therapy?
answer: Unmet childhood needs can make receiving care feel strangely exposing. If you learned that needing comfort led to rejection, criticism, or being ignored, shame may surface in therapy precisely when someone finally offers the attention you needed. The difficult distinction is that feeling ashamed doesn't mean you're doing something wrong; it may mean you're encountering an unfamiliar kind of safety. I've explored this connection further in other writing on my profile.
